# Intake Brief — Ensure all staff effects are implemented (MS-0MW4YAV24001Z7C6)

## Problem statement

Every staff card advertises an ability, and that ability is truthful only when it is backed by card data **and** applied by the engine. Nothing currently guarantees that pairing: the shipped `card-data.csv` compiles but an advertised effect can be description-only (a no-op). The audit performed for this intake inspected all 26 shipped staff templates plus the shipped pack staff and found **one** gap — the **Bookkeeper** advertises "Reduces this business ongoing cost by 20%" but has no backing card-data value, no parser support and no engine consumer, so the printed ability is not the ability the player gets. This item delivers the audit as a durable, reproducible artefact and creates a high-priority work item for every gap so none is silently lost.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — reads a staff card's printed ability and expects it to apply where the engine charges income, reputation, cost or incident damage.
- **Designer / balancer** — needs every staff ability backed by a `card-data.csv` value so economy tuning is trustworthy.
- **Developer / QA** — needs an authoritative audit trail and a regression guard so a missing effect fails the build instead of silently doing nothing.

### User stories

- As a player, I can trust that a staff card's printed ability is the ability I actually get.
- As a designer, every staff effect is backed by a data column/spec and a named engine consumer.
- As a developer, any staff effect that is not fully implemented is tracked as a high-priority work item, and the audit can be re-run when staff are added.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Full audit recorded.** Every shipped staff template (26 base in `src/card-data.csv` plus the shipped pack staff such as `stf-ms-residential-community-gardener`) is inspected and tabulated with: card id, advertised ability, backing card-data field/spec, engine consumer, and implemented/not status. The audit is stored durably (this work item's description and/or a `docs/game/` audit page) and is reviewable.
2. **Every gap has a high-priority work item.** Each staff effect found not fully implemented is captured as a high-priority work item with testable ACs. For the audit's single finding, the Bookkeeper gap is tracked as `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`. No identified gap is left untracked.
3. **Audit is reproducible.** A documented procedure (or script) can re-run the audit against the current card data so future staff additions are checked the same way.
4. **Regression guard extended.** The staff cost-text/data consistency guard (`tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts`) is extended so a percentage-based staff cost-reduction description with no backing data fails the build (delivered with the Bookkeeper gap item, or here).
5. **Documentation updated.** The staff documentation (`docs/game/card-catalog.md`, and the audit page if added) reflects the audit and its findings. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A player can trust that every staff card's printed ability is real: the audit proves the roster is covered and the one broken ability (the Bookkeeper) is now captured as a high-priority, actionable work item instead of quietly misleading the player.

## Constraints

- **Audit only — no effect implementations here.** Effect fixes belong to the gap work items (e.g. `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`). Keep this item's changes to the audit artefact, the gap-item creation and the guard/documentation.
- **Evidence-based.** Record a file:line or data-cell reference for each card's "implemented" verdict; a verdict without evidence is not accepted.
- **Do not rebalance** any coin/reputation value.
- **Minimal churn** — do not restructure the staff system.
- **Determinism** — no RNG changes.

### Out of scope

- Implementing the Bookkeeper effect (tracked in `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`).
- Rebalancing staff costs/values.
- Broad refactors of the buff/ongoing-cost subsystems beyond what the audit and guard need.

## Existing state

The audit was performed during this intake by reading `src/card-data.csv`, the staff parsers (`MainStreetCardsTemplates.parseStaffEffect`), the buff/ongoing-cost helpers (`MainStreetStaffBuffs`) and their engine consumers. Result: **26/27 shipped staff are data-backed and engine-consumed; exactly one (Bookkeeper) is not.**

| Staff | Advertised ability | Backing data | Engine consumer | Status |
|-------|-------------------|--------------|-----------------|--------|
| `staff-assistant` | +2 hand slots | `handSlotsAdded=2` | `maxHandSize` (WeekStart / AiStrategy) | ✅ |
| `staff-manager` | +1 hand slot, +1 action | `handSlotsAdded=1`, `actionsPerTurn=1` | WeekStart / CompetitiveTurn | ✅ |
| `staff-director` | +3 hand slots, +1 action | `handSlotsAdded=3`, `actionsPerTurn=1` | WeekStart / CompetitiveTurn | ✅ |
| `staff-apprentice` | +1 hand slot | `handSlotsAdded=1` | `maxHandSize` | ✅ |
| `staff-executive` | +2 actions | `actionsPerTurn=2` | WeekStart / CompetitiveTurn | ✅ |
| `staff-socialite` | +1 hand slot, +10 rep/turn | `handSlotsAdded=1`, `reputationPerTurn=10` | `applyIncome` (AdjacencyScoring) | ✅ |
| `staff-accountant` | +1 hand slot, refresh −100, Tax 25% | `handSlotsAdded=1`, `refreshCostDiscount=100`, `taxAuditRate=0.25` | `refreshMarketCost`, `computeTaxAuditRate` | ✅ |
| `staff-general-manager` | +1 action, +4 hand slots | `actionsPerTurn=1`, `handSlotsAdded=4` | WeekStart / CompetitiveTurn | ✅ |
| `staff-lookout` | peek once/turn | `peekOncePerTurn=1` | `hasPeekCapableStaff` / EngineActions | ✅ |
| `staff-barista` | +20 coins each adjacent Food | `effect=income:adjacent:20:Food` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-security` | −10% incident coin (own+adjacent) | `effect=incident-coin:cluster:10` | `computeBusinessIncidentMitigation` | ✅ |
| `staff-marketing` | +10% reputation own business | `effect=reputation:percent:10` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-bookkeeper` | −20% ongoing cost own business | **none** | **none** | ❌ **GAP → `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`** |
| `staff-customer-rep` | +10 rep each adjacent business | `effect=reputation:adjacent:10` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-it` | +1 synergy range | `effect=synergy-range:1` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-health-safety` | −10% incident frequency own | `effect=incident-frequency:own:10` | `computeIncidentFrequencyReduction` | ✅ |
| `staff-event-planner` | +100 coins each adjacent Entertainment | `effect=income:adjacent:100:Entertainment` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-delivery` | −50 adjacent purchases | `effect=purchase-discount:adjacent:50` | `computeAdjacentPurchaseDiscount` | ✅ |
| `staff-pr` | +15 rep own business | `effect=reputation:own:15` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-financial` | −100 upgrade cost own business | `upgradeCostDiscount=100` | `computeUpgradeCostDiscount` | ✅ |
| `staff-maintenance` | −50 incident rep (cluster) | `effect=incident-reputation:cluster:50` | `computeBusinessIncidentMitigation` | ✅ |
| `staff-investor` | free reroll/turn, 75% bias | `freeMarketRerollPerTurn=1`, `marketRelevanceBias=0.75` | `MainStreetMarketRefill` | ✅ |
| `staff-florist` | +30 coins adjacent Commerce/Culture | `effect=income:adjacent:30:Commerce\|Culture` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-baker` | +25 coins own business | `effect=income:own:25` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-chef` | +20% income own business | `effect=income:percent:20` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `staff-mechanic` | +30 coins own business | `effect=income:own:30` | `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` | ✅ |
| `stf-ms-residential-community-gardener` (pack) | +1 hand slot | `handSlotsAdded=1` | `maxHandSize` | ✅ |

Additional observations (not gaps): the Bookkeeper escapes the existing cost-text guard because `UNREGISTERED_COST_REDUCTION_RE` deliberately excludes percentage amounts; that guard hole is folded into the Bookkeeper gap item's AC4.

## Desired change

- Record the audit above as the durable artefact (this description and/or a `docs/game/staff-effect-audit.md` page).
- Add a short documented re-run procedure (a script or a checklist of the parser/buff/consumer files) so the audit is reproducible.
- Extend the staff cost-text guard to detect percentage-based ongoing-cost descriptions with no backing data (via the Bookkeeper gap item or here).
- Keep the Bookkeeper gap work item `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY` linked and high priority.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — link/append the audit reference so the roster points at the audit.
- `docs/game/staff-effect-audit.md` (new, optional) — the durable audit table + re-run procedure.
- `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — percentage-aware guard (if delivered here).
- `src/card-data.csv` — read-only source of the audit (no changes here).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`, `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — read-only consumers verified by the audit.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: the audit silently misses a gap** because a card's effect is partially wired (e.g. data exists but no consumer, or a consumer reads a different field). Mitigation: every "implemented" verdict cites both the data cell and the consumer symbol, and the guard/re-run procedure keeps it honest.
- **Risk: scope creep into implementation** — the audit item starts fixing effects instead of recording/tracking them. Mitigation: the audit item is explicitly audit + delegation; effect code belongs to gap items (e.g. `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`).
- **Risk: future packs regress untracked.** Mitigation: the reproducible re-run procedure covers pack staff.
- **Assumption:** "all staff" = the shipped base roster plus shipped pack staff; dynamically authored future packs are covered by the re-run procedure.
- **Assumption:** this item is audit + delegation; the Bookkeeper fix is tracked in `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`.
- **Assumption:** computing an effect's "implemented" status from data-cell + consumer-symbol evidence is sufficient (no runtime execution of every effect in this item).

## Related work

- **MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY** (open, high) — the single gap this audit found: Bookkeeper −20% ongoing-cost effect not implemented (`discovered-from:` this item).
- **MS-0MW3JXF6U00753LB** (completed) — two-type staff redesign that wired the per-business `effect` specs and their consumers; left the Bookkeeper without a spec.
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** (completed) — precedent for backfilling a description-only staff effect end-to-end with a guard.
- **MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z** (completed) — staff description ×100 consistency; created the guard extended here.
- **MS-0MW2XKTR50062OFL** (completed) — GDD staff consistency verification (a sibling consistency-check pattern to mirror for reproducibility).
- **CG-0MT4WXNR80090FXZ** — specialization applicant wave that introduced the Bookkeeper.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No blocking questions. The seed context ("iterate over all staff, inspect the code, create high-priority work items for gaps") fully defines the audit deliverable, and the repo provided all evidence needed. **Assumption recorded:** this item is an *audit + delegation* task — effect fixes live in the gap work items (the Bookkeeper fix is `MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY`), not in this item. **Assumption recorded:** "all staff" means the shipped base roster plus shipped pack staff; dynamically authored future packs are covered by the reproducible re-run procedure rather than individually audited here.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MW7D0LGL007PAUY** – Bookkeeper -20% ongoing-cost staff effect is not implemented (open)
- **MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND** – Staff effects are not implemented (open)
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** – Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ability, ac4, acceptance, accepted, action (+283 more)
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — matched: 0mw3jxf6u00753lb, ability, acceptance, accountant, action (+250 more)

# Clicking to close the end-of-turn ledger selects the card below

## Problem statement

Pressing an action button on the end-of-turn ledger (the **Turn Summary** dialog — `[ Next Turn ]`, and by extension `[ Bank Loan ]`) also selects the hand card rendered underneath it. Closing the ledger should only resume the deferred closing; it must leave the hand untouched.

## Users

- **The human player, at the end of every day** — has just reviewed their P&L statement and presses `[ Next Turn ]` to start the next day.
  - *As a player closing the end-of-turn ledger, I want the hand to be exactly as I left it, so that I do not start the next day with an accidental card selection or an unexpected "placing from hand" state.*
- **A player who ends the day with a full hand** — the hand row is directly under the ledger's action row, so this is the common case, not an edge case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pressing `[ Next Turn ]` on the Turn Summary dialog dismisses the ledger and starts the next day **without** selecting, highlighting, or entering a "placing from hand" / "event selected" state for any hand card (`pendingHandIndex` stays `null`, `uiPhase` returns to `market`, and no card is bought, moved, played, or discarded).
- Pressing `[ Bank Loan ]` (enabled) opens the mid-game loan selector and likewise never changes hand-card selection; cancelling back to the summary leaves the hand untouched.
- The fix holds when the ledger's action button geometrically overlaps a hand card (the normal layout: the middle hand card sits directly under `[ Next Turn ]`), and for both mouse and touch input.
- A regression test reproduces the defect in a real Phaser scene: it positions a hand card under the ledger's action button, dispatches a real pointer press/release at the button, asserts the closing resumes (or the loan selector opens) **and** asserts the hand-card selection state is unchanged.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Closing the end-of-turn ledger no longer selects a hand card, so every new day starts with a clean hand and no accidental placement state.

## Constraints

- The Turn Summary dialog is the only gate in front of the deferred closing: `[ Next Turn ]` must remain the sole way to resume it, and the enabled/disabled `[ Bank Loan ]` matrix, tab switching and keyboard navigation must keep working exactly as today.
- Overlay-pattern compliance (AGENTS.md UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` from `@ui`, all elements parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths 199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (elements), everything tracked in `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance (no fade — reduced-motion safe).
- The fix must not weaken the deliberate click-through protections elsewhere (tutorial tooltip DOMElement isolation, `CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV`) or the drag-drop click-vs-drag thresholds.
- No new engine/state semantics: this is a presentation/input bug; the closing economy and ledger figures must be untouched.
- Reduced-motion, replay/headless and competitive paths must keep their current pacing and behaviour.

## Existing state

- The Turn Summary dialog is rendered by `presentTurnSummaryPanel()` in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`. The panel is `PANEL_WIDTH = 680` × `PANEL_HEIGHT = 640`, centred on the 1280×720 scene (`panelY ≈ 40`, bottom ≈ 680).
- Its action row sits at `btnY = panelY + PANEL_H - 62 ≈ 618`, with `[ Next Turn ]` at `centerX - 120 ≈ (520, 618)` and `[ Bank Loan ]` at `centerX + 120 ≈ (760, 618)`.
- The hand row is centred on `columnCenterX ≈ 467` with `handY ≈ 628` and `handCardH = 80`, so hand cards span roughly y 590–666 and x 251–683 (three 140 px cards at ≈ 319 / 467 / 615). **`[ Next Turn ]` therefore sits directly over the middle hand card.**
- The action buttons act on `pointerdown` (`nextTurnBtn.on('pointerdown', …)` → `dismissPanel()` then `handlers.onNextTurn()`). The hand's business/upgrade cards act on `pointerup` in the drag-drop path (`container.on('pointerup', …)` → `onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick`), and the closing's `advanceTurn` starts the next day only after a bounded wait (`s.time.delayedCall(800, …)` or the bounded income-collection deferral).
- Working hypothesis to confirm during implementation: the button's `pointerdown` destroys the button and the full-screen input-blocking backdrop, so the matching `pointerup` hit-tests against the now-uncovered hand card beneath and its click-to-select handler fires. Because the button overlaps the card, this is repeatable for the common full-hand case.
- Related work already shipped: the tabbed P&L Turn Summary (`MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY`), the turn-summary gate (`MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R`), the bank-loan button (`MS-0MVXYCICT0051LU7`), and the tutorial tooltip click-through fix (`CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV`).

## Desired change

- Make the ledger's action buttons consume the complete press/release cycle so a `[ Next Turn ]` / `[ Bank Loan ]` press can never be interpreted as a hand-card click, even when the button overlaps the hand row.
- Alternatively (or additionally), ensure the hand layer cannot receive pointer events while the Turn Summary overlay is presented — without blocking the overlay's own controls.
- Keep the ledger's layout, values, tab strip, keyboard navigation and the `[ Next Turn ]`-only resume contract unchanged.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the reported control is `[ Next Turn ]` in the Turn Summary dialog (the "end-of-turn ledger"); the same renderer serves the competitive panel, so the fix must cover both.
- **Risk — over-blocking:** a blunt "disable the hand layer while any overlay is up" change could break legitimate hand interactions after dismissal, or the drag-drop manager's registered draggables. Prefer a scoped guard that only suppresses hand clicks during the ledger's own press, and restore it on dismissal.
- **Risk — button responsiveness:** moving the action buttons from `pointerdown` to `pointerup` would change the press feel and could interact with the drag thresholds; if chosen, cover it with the existing dialog browser tests.
- **Risk — layout regression:** shrinking or moving the panel to avoid the hand row must keep every statement line, the tab strip and the `[ Bank Loan ]` hint on-screen at 1280×720 (and the reduced-motion/instant-appearance contract).
- **Scope-creep guard:** anything beyond "the ledger's action must not select a hand card" (e.g. a general overlay-input audit, or tooltip behaviour in the ledger — `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO`) is a separate work item, not this fix.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` — the dialog renderer: action buttons (`[ Next Turn ]`, `[ Bank Loan ]`), dismissal, overlay objects; the primary fix site.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `presentTurnSummaryGate()` / `advanceTurn()` / `finishTurnPresentation()`; the closing that the button resumes.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — hand-card `pointerup` click handlers (`onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick`) and the drag-drop registration; the leaked event's destination.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — `onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick` / `onHandEventCardClick` and their `uiPhase` gates.
- `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts` / `core/src/ui/OverlayButton.ts` — shared backdrop/button factories and their input behaviour.
- `core/src/ui/HandView.ts` — hand layout (card positions) and interactive card sprites.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` — existing overlay browser coverage to extend.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-gate.test.ts` — existing gate coverage.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Turn Summary dialog + closing gate documentation (update the interaction contract).

## Related work

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — End of Turn summary dialog (parent epic; completed).
- `MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY` — Turn summary as a P&L statement (completed).
- `MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R` — Turn Summary gate (completed).
- `MS-0MVXYCICT0051LU7` / `MS-0MVXYCJCK006UE62` — Bank Loan button and its enabled/disabled matrix (completed).
- `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` — Refactor end-of-turn presentation (completed).
- `MS-0MV767QTO008JUDJ` — Clicking a selected hand card deselects it (completed; same selection state).
- `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO` — Tooltips in the end-of-turn ledger (open; same dialog).
- `CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV` — Tutorial tooltip pointer pass-through fix (completed; same class of click-through defect).
- Repository docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (Turn Summary dialog + closing gate), `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were needed. The seed report ("When I click on the button to close the end of turn ledger, the card in my hand below the button is selected. It should not be.") identifies the dialog (the Turn Summary / end-of-turn ledger), the trigger (its action button) and the defect (hand-card selection) unambiguously, and repo research resolved the rest.
- Q: "Which control is 'the button to close the end of turn ledger'?" — Answer (agent research): the `[ Next Turn ]` button in the Turn Summary dialog (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`). Evidence: `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO` uses "end-of-turn ledger" to mean the Turn Summary dialog; the dialog's only close/resume control is `[ Next Turn ]`.
- Q: "Is the defect a layout overlap or an input-handling leak?" — Answer (agent research, to be confirmed during implementation): both are present — the action row geometrically overlaps the middle hand card, and the button dismisses the overlay on `pointerdown` so the matching `pointerup` can reach the hand card. Evidence: computed panel/hand geometry and the `pointerdown` / `pointerup` handlers above.
- Assumption (documented): the primary target is single-player play; the competitive per-seat panel uses the same renderer and `[ Next Turn ]` button, so the fix should cover it too.

# Intake Brief — Staff effects: define, implement, and verify all staff cards (MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND)

## Problem statement

Staff cards are the management layer of the Main Street economy: 26 shipped templates across two staff types (17 business staff, 9 management-company staff), each with a documented effect in GDD Appendix D.4. The producer reports that staff effects do not appear to be implemented in play. A code review for this intake shows the picture is uneven rather than uniformly broken: most effects are wired and tested, but at least one documented effect (the Bookkeeper's −20% own-business ongoing-cost reduction) has no card data, no parser support and no engine wiring, and the card-level verification suite reports every staff card as `pass` while exercising only a subset of effects. The result is that neither the player nor the team can trust that a staff card's printed ability actually happens.

## Review findings (evidence gathered during intake)

| Area | Finding | Evidence |
|------|---------|----------|
| Business-staff per-business buffs | Wired for income, reputation, synergy range, purchase discount and incident mitigation | `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`, `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` |
| Management-company effects | Hand slots, actions/turn, refresh discount, tax-audit override, peek and free market re-roll are all consumed by the engine | `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` |
| Bookkeeper (−20% ongoing cost) | **Not implemented**: `staff-bookkeeper` has an empty `effect` cell, `parseStaffEffect` has no `ongoing-cost` dimension, `StaffCard` has no per-business ongoing-cost field, and `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` applies only the management-company Cost Cutter reduction | `src/card-data.csv`, `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`, `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` |
| Card-level verification | `verifyStaffCard` asserts hire cost, hand slots, legacy purchase discount, refresh discount, tax rate, actions and peek — it does **not** assert per-business buffs, `reputationPerTurn`, `adjacencyPurchaseDiscount`, `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`/`marketRelevanceBias`, or the Bookkeeper effect, yet every staff row is marked `unitTestStatus = pass` | `tests/main-street/cards/definitions/runners.ts`, `src/card-data.csv` |
| Behavioural tests | Good coverage exists for most business-staff roles and several management-company roles, but it is spread across many files and is not one-per-card | `tests/main-street/staff-two-type-redesign.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `investor-staff.test.ts`, `MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts` |

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — needs each hired staff card to deliver the ability printed on it, at the stated magnitude and scope, so hiring is a real economic trade-off.
- **Main Street player (learning)** — needs the card text, card tooltip and actual behaviour to agree, so the rules are teachable.
- **Game designer / balance owner** — needs a single auditable statement of which staff effects are implemented and tested, so balance changes rest on real behaviour.
- **Implementing developer** — needs one clearly scoped verification/fix item per staff card so gaps cannot hide behind a blanket `pass`.

Example user stories:

- As a player, I want the Baker to add exactly +25 coins/turn to the business that employs it, so that its salary is a calculable return.
- As a player, I want the Bookkeeper to reduce only its own business's ongoing cost by 20%, so that the printed ability actually happens.
- As a developer, I want a failing test when a staff card's documented effect is missing or mis-scoped, so that a card cannot ship as a no-op.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A card-by-card implementation audit of all 26 shipped staff templates is recorded, stating for each card the documented effect, the parsing path, the engine wiring and the behavioural test, and listing every gap found.
- Every staff card's documented effect (GDD Appendix D.4.3/D.4.4) is implemented end-to-end and observable in gameplay; in particular the Bookkeeper's −20% own-business ongoing-cost reduction is implemented in card data, parsed into a typed field, applied per business during the ongoing-cost phase, and floored at 0.
- Each of the 26 staff cards has at least one automated behavioural test that asserts its documented effect and scope (own business vs. 8-way neighbours vs. player/street), rather than only asserting that the card can be hired.
- The card-level CSV verification (`unitTestStatus`) reflects the behavioural assertion, so a card whose effect is absent or unimplemented cannot report `pass`.
- At least one testing/validation criterion is satisfied by the above behavioural tests running in the project suite and failing on a missing or mis-scoped effect.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD Appendix D.4, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` where affected).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can trust that every hired staff card delivers the ability printed on it, so hiring decisions — and the salaries paid for them — become a reliable economic trade-off instead of a gamble on whether the effect is wired.

## Constraints

- The two-type staff model (business staff vs. management-company staff) and the scope gate in `MainStreetStaffBuffs` are authoritative; do not reintroduce street-wide effects for business staff or per-business effects for management-company staff.
- Staff effects must remain deterministic given the seeded RNG (Investor re-roll bias, Lookout peek, Health & Safety Inspector avert).
- The `card-data.csv` header set is validated against card packs; prefer encoding the Bookkeeper effect in the existing `effect` column grammar (e.g. a new `ongoing-cost:percent:20` dimension) rather than adding a column.
- The caching-safety contract holds: staff buffs are derived at call time and never written into `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn`.
- No balance value changes are in scope unless the audit finds a documented effect that is genuinely wrong; this epic is about definition + implementation + verification.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv` carries 26 staff rows; the business-staff per-business effects ride in the `effect` column (`income:`, `reputation:`, `synergy-range:`, `purchase-discount:`, `incident-*`), while management-company effects ride in dedicated columns (`handSlotsAdded`, `actionsPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `taxAuditRate`, `peekOncePerTurn`, `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`, `marketRelevanceBias`).
- `staff-bookkeeper` is the only shipped staff row with no effect data, despite the GDD and card catalog documenting −20% ongoing cost.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` exposes pure buff helpers; `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` folds them into the income and reputation phases; `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` deducts ongoing costs (currently with only the street-wide Cost Cutter reduction).
- `tests/main-street/cards/definitions/runners.ts::verifyStaffCard` is the shared card-level verifier; it marks rows `pass` without asserting most per-business effects.

## Desired change

- Produce the full audit, then close every gap: implement the Bookkeeper effect end-to-end and fix any further gaps the audit surfaces.
- Make per-card behaviour verification complete: one child work item per shipped staff card (26 children), each confirming the card is properly defined (data, type, description) and behaves as documented, adding or tightening the behavioural test that proves it. The audit/consolidation work is the first child; the per-card children depend on it.
- Make the card-level `unitTestStatus` honest: a card reports `pass` only when its documented effect is exercised.
- Keep the two-type model, scope gate, determinism and caching guarantees intact.

**Note on delivery model:** decomposition into one child per staff card is a planning-stage action (the `plan` skill creates the children); this epic defines the scope and acceptance criteria they must collectively satisfy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — add a typed per-business ongoing-cost reduction field to `StaffCard` and document its scope.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — extend `parseStaffEffect` with the `ongoing-cost` dimension and validate the spec.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — add a pure per-business ongoing-cost-reduction helper (sum of employing staff, no street leakage).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — apply the Bookkeeper reduction inside `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` per slot, floored at 0.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — confirm buff folding order stays consistent (only if the audit finds a change is needed).
- `tests/main-street/staff-two-type-redesign.test.ts` — extend behavioural coverage for business-staff cards.
- `tests/main-street/cards/definitions/runners.ts` — make `verifyStaffCard` assert per-business buffs, `reputationPerTurn`, `adjacencyPurchaseDiscount`, and the free market re-roll/Bias; fail on a card with no asserted effect.
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` — keep the authoritative staff docs in step with the implementation.

## Related work

- MS-0MW4YAV24001Z7C6 — Ensure all staff effects are implemented (overlapping intent, narrower scope; this epic supersedes it for definition and per-card decomposition)
- MS-0MW3JXF6U00753LB — Implement two-type staff redesign deltas in card data and engine (completed; established the per-business `effect` grammar)
- MS-0MW4MSNWR00123OZ — Implement: scope gate in buff aggregation functions (completed)
- MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O — Staff impact (completed; GDD two-type redesign)
- MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z — Fix staff description text for ×100 consistency (completed; noted the IT Specialist / Delivery Driver gaps that were since closed)
- MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M — Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (completed)
- Docs: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (Appendix D.4), `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/specialization-skills.md`, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed description, GDD Appendix D.4, the shipped card data and the code review gave sufficient detail to define the epic. The entries below record the evidence-backed answers to the implicit questions a producer would ask.

- Q: "Are all staff effects really unimplemented?" — Answer (code review, this session): No. Most are wired and tested; the Bookkeeper's −20% ongoing cost is the clear unimplemented effect, and the card-level verifier does not assert most effects. Source: `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`, `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/card-data.csv`, `tests/main-street/cards/definitions/runners.ts`.
- Q: "What is the authoritative design for each staff card?" — Answer: GDD Appendix D.4.3/D.4.4 and `docs/game/card-catalog.md`. Source: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` lines 526–665.
- Q: "Should business-staff effects ever be street-wide?" — Answer: No; the two-type scope gate forbids it. Source: MS-0MW3JXF6U00753LB, MS-0MW4MSNWR00123OZ, GDD D.4.8 §2/§4.
- Q: "Is the Bookkeeper effect a data-only fix?" — Answer: No; it needs a typed field, a parser dimension and engine wiring in `applyBusinessOngoingCosts`, because no per-business ongoing-cost field exists today. Source: `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`, `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`.
- Q: "How many children should the epic have?" — Answer: One per shipped staff card (26), plus an audit/consolidation child, created at plan time. Source: producer description ("create a child for every staff card").
- **OPEN QUESTION** — Decomposition breadth: the Producer description asks for a child for *every* staff card (26), but the code review found most effects already implemented and tested; should the plan stage create all 26 per-card verification children, or only children for cards with a real gap (plus the audit)? **Recommended:** all 26 — a complete one-per-card audit trail is the stated intent, and it surfaces regressions that current tests miss.
- **OPEN QUESTION** — Overlapping item: MS-0MW4YAV24001Z7C6 ("Ensure all staff effects are implemented") expresses the same intent at a narrower scope. # Intake Brief — Bookkeeper −20% ongoing-cost staff effect is not implemented

## Problem statement

`staff-bookkeeper` (Bookkeeper) advertises "Keeps the books tight. Reduces this business ongoing cost by 20%." in `src/card-data.csv` and `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, but the effect is not backed by any card-data field or engine path: the shipped row has an empty `effect` spec and no dedicated column, `parseStaffEffect` does not understand an `ongoing-cost` dimension, and neither `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` nor the competitive per-owner path applies a per-business percentage reduction. The printed ability is therefore not the ability the player gets. This item closes that gap (found by the audit in `MS-0MW4YAV24001Z7C6`).

## Users

- **Main Street player** — employs the Bookkeeper and expects their business's ongoing cost to drop by 20%.
- **Designer / balancer** — needs every staff ability backed by a data column so economy tuning is trustworthy.
- **Developer / QA** — needs the effect implemented once, in the shared ongoing-cost paths, with a regression guard so it cannot silently drift again.

### User stories

- As a player, when I employ a Bookkeeper at one of my Commerce/Food/Service businesses, that business's running cost is 20% lower.
- As a designer, the Bookkeeper's printed −20% is backed by a card-data value and consumed by the engine.
- As a developer, a future percentage-based staff cost effect without a backing field fails the build.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Data representation added.** The Bookkeeper's −20% ongoing-cost reduction is carried by the card data — either a new `effect` spec dimension (`ongoing-cost:own:20`) parsed by `parseStaffEffect`, or a dedicated staff column — and the Bookkeeper's row in `src/card-data.csv` is updated so the value is non-empty and matches the description (20).
2. **Per-business engine consumer.** The reduction is applied to the employing business's `ongoingCost` only, in both the single-player `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` path and the competitive `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` per-owner path, before the street-wide Cost Cutter reduction; the effective cost is floored at 0 and stacking with the Cost Cutter follows the documented integer-rounding convention.
3. **Scope correctness.** Only the business employing the Bookkeeper benefits; neighbours and non-employing businesses are unaffected. The effect is inert for a bookkeeper held but not employed.
4. **Regression guard extended.** `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` registers the Bookkeeper contract and its percentage-aware detector catches an ongoing-cost percentage description with no backing data, so the gap cannot silently return.
5. **Tests.** Unit tests cover: single-player reduction, competitive per-owner reduction, clamp at 0, no effect on non-employing businesses, stacking with Cost Cutter, and the extended guard; all new/updated tests pass.
6. **Documentation updated.** `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (Bookkeeper row/rationale) and `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` (if relevant) reflect the implemented mechanic; code comments explain the data spec and consumer. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Determinism preserved.** No new RNG consumption; headless/AI parity and seeded determinism unchanged.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A player who hires the Bookkeeper now actually pays 20% less to run its business, so the card's printed promise matches the game's behaviour instead of being a no-op.

## Constraints

- **Per-business scope.** The description says "this business" — do not silently make it street-wide. Apply only to the employing business's own `ongoingCost`.
- **Source of truth is `card-data.csv`.** Do not hand-rebalance unrelated values.
- **Reuse the shared ongoing-cost paths.** Do not add a parallel deduction path; extend `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` and `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`.
- **Minimal churn** — touch only the Bookkeeper effect, its parser, its consumers and its tests/docs.

### Out of scope

- Rebalancing any other coin/reputation value.
- Evaluating or changing any other staff effect (covered by the parent audit `MS-0MW4YAV24001Z7C6`).
- Adding a general "any percentage staff effect" framework beyond what this one card needs.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv` `staff-bookkeeper`: `cost=300`, `ongoingCost=50`, `tier=2`, `allowedBusinessTypes=Commerce|Food|Service`, description "Keeps the books tight. Reduces this business ongoing cost by 20%.", `effect` column **empty**.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` `parseStaffEffect` understands `income`, `reputation`, `synergy-range`, `purchase-discount` and `incident-*` dimensions only — no `ongoing-cost`.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs` reduces ongoing cost only via the street-wide `skill-cost-cutter` (`COST_CUTTER_ONGOING_PCT = 0.15`); `computeStreetOngoingCostReductionPct` is street-wide.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` sums all placed businesses' `ongoingCost`, then applies the street-wide Cost Cutter reduction; there is no per-business percentage reduction. `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` mirrors this per owner.
- `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` excludes percentages from its `UNREGISTERED_COST_REDUCTION_RE`, so the Bookkeeper's "20%" is not currently guarded.
- No existing test exercises the Bookkeeper effect.

## Desired change

- Add a machine-readable `ongoing-cost:own:20` effect spec (or dedicated column) and parse it into the `StaffCard`.
- Apply the per-business reduction to the employing business's `ongoingCost` in both ongoing-cost paths, floored at 0 and composed with the street-wide Cost Cutter.
- Extend the description↔data guard to cover percentage-based ongoing-cost effects.
- Add unit tests for single-player, competitive, clamp, scope and stacking; update the card catalog/docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — `staff-bookkeeper` gains a non-empty `effect` value (e.g. `ongoing-cost:own:20`).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — add the parsed ongoing-cost field to `StaffCard`.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the new `ongoing-cost` dimension in `parseStaffEffect`.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — per-business ongoing-cost helper (mirroring `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` scope) or extend the buff bundle.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — apply the per-business reduction in `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` and `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`.
- `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — register the Bookkeeper contract; percentage-aware detector.
- `tests/main-street/` — new tests for the effect (single + competitive + clamp + scope + stacking).
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — Bookkeeper row/rationale.
- `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` — note the implemented mechanic if relevant.

## Related work

- **MS-0MW4YAV24001Z7C6** (in-progress) — parent audit "Ensure all staff effects are implemented"; this item is the single gap it found (`discovered-from:`).
- **MS-0MW3JXF6U00753LB** (completed) — two-type staff redesign wired the per-business `effect` specs (income/reputation/synergy-range/purchase-discount/incident) and their consumers; the Bookkeeper was left without a spec.
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** (completed) — precedent: implementing a previously description-only staff effect (IT Specialist / Delivery Driver) end-to-end with a data column, engine consumer and guard.
- **MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z** (completed) — staff description ×100 consistency; created the guard this item extends.
- **CG-0MT4WXNR80090FXZ** — specialization applicant wave that introduced the Bookkeeper.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No blocking questions. The audit (`MS-0MW4YAV24001Z7C6`) established the gap, and the expectation is taken directly from the shipped description ("Reduces this business ongoing cost by 20%") and the parent item's instruction to create a high-priority work item for it. Assumption recorded: the reduction is per-business (the employing business only), matching "this business", and is expressed as a machine-readable `effect` spec to follow the established per-business staff-effect grammar.
